answer: The verifier issues a traversal proof: the agent reserves a 40 GB RAM array, then walks its cache lines across pseudo-random offsets tied to a comet nonce, touching each 64-byte line inside 400 ns. One traversal costs about $0.30 of reserved memory. One honest agent walks its own array once, while ten fakes need ten 40 GB arrays and ten controllers, so the mesa bill grows tenfold. The chain checks the traversal hash, slashes the bond of any node skipping lines or replaying a stale proof, and freezes repeat offenders, logging the plume failure on-ledger.
